newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods - Gasoline on the go in ebb and flow.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods - Gasoline on the go in ebb and flow.

text.p: U.S. cash gasoline markets, fresh following Monday's respite that saw weakening of values in the highly volatile Gulf Coast market, were again on the go Tuesday, traders said.

There did not appear to be any major factors behind the firming of differentials both at the Gulf and in New York Harbor, which in any case was on the mild side and nothing like the wild blowout seen last Friday at the Gulf.
Midcontinent values, however, were slightly weaker due to sluggish activity.

Still, underlying unleaded futures were leading the way upward on NYMEX amid expectations that this week's report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) will show possibly the last great drawdown of unleaded stocks of the summer.

Heating oil futures were predictably lagging gasoline's gains, but a heat wave sweeping across much of the U.S. was fueling views that the stage is setting for a spike in low sulphur jet fuel values, which often take off in heat waves.
At 1111 EDT/1511 GMT, August NYMEX unleaded was 1.00 cent higher 59.35 cents a gallon and August heating oil was 0.38 cent higher at 52.05 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF

Bellwether "M1" regular conventional southern-grade gasoline was gingerly building on a firming trend that took hold Monday afternoon, though traders were not saying differentials were going through the roof -- yet.
Still it was enough of a move to provide extra fuel for the NYMEX crowd, which was citing Gulf Coast gasoline as the other reason besides the API data for the sharp NYMEX move.
Prompt M1 was talked at between 0.30 and 0.05 cent under August NYMEX unleaded futures, with any month barrels pegged at between 1.75 and 1.50 cents under August futures.
Traders continued to look ahead to Thursday's scheduling deadline for loading product into the Colonial Pipeline in time for for Colonial's front 21st shipping cycle.
Prices often move sharply either up or down in conjunction with Colonial scheduling deadlines, and are thus closely watched as indicators of the market's tone.

Some traders said they would not be surprised to see M1 differentials firm sharply on Thursday, in part because there is lingering suspicion that one Gulf Coast trader who had been short wet supplies is not quite done covering those shorts.
NEW HARBOR
Gasoline was also firming in New York on views supplies were tightening amid a near-term dip in the number of gasoline cargoes, particularly the incremental supplies coming from Western Europe.

Prompt "M2" regular conventional northern-grade was heard done late Monday at 2.00 cents under August unleaded. Dead prompt supplies were assessed at 1.75 under while any month supplies were called between 2.50 and 2.25 cents under.
Those values constituted a firming of anywhere from 0.25 to 0.50 cent from levels heard during Monday's mostly quiet trade.

The cleaner-burning "A2" regular northern-grade reformulated gasoline was meanwhile heard done at 1.00 cent over August NYMEX, or about 0.25 cent firmer than differentials on Monday. At least 100,000 barrels of A2 were said to have changed hands -- a decent volume before midday, traders said.
Regarding the heat wave, some traders were waiting like hawks for phone calls from utilities in the sweltering Northeast looking for low sulphur 55-grade jet fuel.

The 55-grade is used to run auxiliary generators that are used to power the extraordinary demand that hundreds of thousands of humming residentials air conditioning units demand when the mercury approaches 100 degrees fahrenheit (37.77C).
Prompt 55-grade changed hands on Monday at 2.15 cents over August NYMEX heat, but that value was steady with levels pegged on Friday.
MIDCONTINENT

Prompt gasoline differentials in the Midcontinent remained a bit sluggish, dropping slightly amid comfortable inventory levels. Stocks have been running above traditional levels for much of the summer, with the latest reading at 5.8 million barrels in the Explorer Pipeline system, said traders.
In Group Three, prompt gasoline edged down about a quarter cent to 2.50/2.75 cents above August futures, with any month barrels at 2.15/2.25 cents above the print.
Chicago prompt material fell about 0.65 cent amid little demand, with a trade heard done at 1.60 cents. An any-month parcel was heard swapping hands at 1.35 cent over the print.
Distillates, however, gained in Chicago amid sweltering heat, rising a quarter cent to deals done even with the screen.
